starts.note:
customer: start only when the customer asks to dispute one or more debit card transactions. This includes a customer who, during a transaction review in another job, denies a transaction and agrees when the agent advises filing a dispute. Such reviews are a chip/CVV mismatch, a fraud alert, or the PIN lock investigation's check for successful unauthorized transactions on a card that cannot be unlocked.

File one dispute for each transaction the customer names. Card actions (a freeze, or a close and reissue) are not optional offers: they follow from the categories of the disputes actually filed, as the dispute procedure requires. A dispute held back by the open-dispute limit, or dropped by the customer after a record check, sets no card action.

If the customer opens by asking for a human agent, offer to help first, as the policy says, and transfer only on the 4th request.

Bounds from the records: a statement comes after its transactions, so a report within 60 days of the transaction date (get_transactions vs get_time) is also within 60 days of the statement; and a report within 2 business days of the transaction is also within 2 business days of the statement. A statement the customer reviewed when they noticed the charge is dated on or before discovery_date, so a report more than 2 business days after that discovery date is past the 2-business-day window. If the customer is reporting after the 2-business-day window (for example, they say they are reporting late), tell them their maximum liability is $500 while they are within 60 days of the statement, and that any provisional credit is the disputed amount reduced by that liability. All of the following hold:
- Each card in scope has had its action performed (kept active, frozen, or closed with the right reason) and confirmed, or the customer was told what blocks it. Cards in scope are those the customer asked to close, those with filed disputes, and PIN-locked cards the customer agreed to close after the investigation. With several cards, each card was handled on its own.
- A card blocked by pending transactions was not closed. The customer was told it can be closed once the transactions settle (no settlement time promised). It stays frozen if frozen, or was frozen if the customer agreed.
- A PIN-locked card with disputed fraud was closed exactly once.
- A PIN-locked card with no money taken was closed (reason fraud_suspected) only after the customer chose closure, with no dispute filed.
- A card with a pending refund was closed only after the customer acknowledged in writing that the refund goes to the linked checking account. Otherwise the customer was told to wait for the refund to process.
- For a PIN-locked card, the customer has been told whether any money was taken.
- Disputes that were not filed set no card action.
- A card with a fraud alert and a filed fraud dispute was closed without its alert being cleared.
- A card the customer found again was not closed.
- For each closed card, one of these is true: a replacement was ordered to the confirmed address (on file or alternate) with the correct tier fees and timeframe; the customer declined one; or the customer was told when one can be ordered (the Entry 48-hour wait counted from the recorded closure time, including after accepting the excess fee; or the tier limit, with the age-out date when the customer chose to wait).
- Lost and stolen cards have been handed to the cross-product check (once per conversation).

rules: ENTRY tier (Light Blue, Light Green, Green Fee-Free): 48-hour wait after closure, standard shipping only, delivery_fee $0, at most 2 replacements per rolling 12 months
MID tier: at most 3 replacements per rolling 12 months, no waiting period
The CLASSIC design costs $0 at every tier
Premium tier: up to 5 replacements per 12 months, no waiting period, STANDARD and EXPEDITED at $0, RUSH at $35. PREMIUM design $0, CUSTOM $15, CLASSIC $0.
The account must hold at least $25
Cards ship to US domestic addresses only
Entry tier over 2 replacements in 12 months: wait or pay $25
Premium tier over 5 replacements: must wait, with no fee option
Elite tier: every delivery option is free
Elite tier: same-business-day shipping if ordered before 2pm EST
An order fails if the account cannot cover the fees
Shipping, design and excess replacement fees are charged to the linked checking account when the card is ordered
Only cards with issue_reason lost, stolen, fraud or damaged count as replacements toward the tier limit
The limit is per rolling 12 months; the oldest counted replacement ages out 12 months after its date_issued
Mid-tier excess replacements: wait, or pay $15
Premium tier RUSH shipping costs $35
EXPEDITED delivery takes 3-5 business days; RUSH takes 1-2 and costs $35 unless the tier waives it
Elite tier: every card design is free
CLASSIC is the default design with no fee
Elite tier (Bluest) has unlimited replacements
Cards with issue_reason new_account, first_card, expired, upgrade or bank_reissue do not count toward the replacement limit

steps.do: Pick each dispute's dispute_category from that case's own facts. If the same charge posted more than once: 'duplicate_charge'. If the customer was charged a different amount than expected: 'incorrect_amount'. If the customer did not make the transaction, ask whether fraud is suspected. If yes: 'card_present_fraud' for an in-store or physical transaction, 'card_not_present_fraud' for an online, phone or other card-not-present transaction. If no (for example a family member, or a forgotten transaction): 'unauthorized_transaction'. If the ATM dispensed the wrong amount or no cash: 'atm_cash_discrepancy'. If an ATM deposit was not credited: 'atm_deposit_not_credited'. If the customer paid and never received the item or service: 'goods_services_not_received'. If a subscription was cancelled but still charged: 'recurring_charge_after_cancellation'.
